subject: Physics
topic: Rest and motion: why motion depends on the observer
title: Rest and Motion: Motion is Relative
summary: Are you moving right now? It depends on who is watching. Rest and motion are always measured from a reference point.
keyPoints: An object is **at rest** if its position does not change with time, relative to a reference point.
It is **in motion** if its position changes with time, relative to that point.
The same object can be at rest for one observer and moving for another.
Nothing is in absolute rest: even the ground moves with the Earth around the Sun.

blocks.p: Sitting in a moving train, are you at rest or moving? Both answers are right, because **rest and motion are relative**: they mean nothing until you choose a **reference point** (an observer or origin) to measure position from.

blocks.alt: A train with you and a friend inside, and a person on the platform
blocks.caption: Your friend sees you at rest; the person on the platform sees you moving.

head: Term
Meaning
rows: A fixed point (or observer) from which position is measured; also called the origin.
Position does not change with time, relative to the reference point.
Position changes with time, relative to the reference point.

blocks.formula: Position changes with time → motion.   Position does not change → rest.

list: Passengers in a bus are at rest relative to each other but moving relative to the road.
A tree is at rest relative to the ground but moving relative to the Sun.
A geostationary satellite stays over one spot of Earth, yet moves fast relative to the Sun.

blocks.p: **Common mistake:** saying something is simply "at rest" or "moving". Always name the reference point. Slow motion is still motion if the position changes.

quiz.q: A girl sits in a moving car. Relative to the car she is:
options: both at rest and in motion
quiz.explain: Her position inside the car does not change, so relative to the car she is at rest (relative to the road she is moving).

quiz.q: What must you choose before calling an object "at rest"?
quiz.explain: Rest and motion are relative: you first need a reference point to measure position from.

options: Relative to the Earth yes; relative to the Sun no
quiz.explain: Its position does not change relative to the ground, but the Earth carries it around the Sun.

quiz.q: An object is in motion when its position:
options: changes with time relative to a reference point
quiz.explain: Motion means the position changes with time, measured from a chosen reference point.

simulation.reason: Switching the observer and watching the same passenger stay still or move is the heart of this idea; students can test it themselves instead of only being told.
simulation.objective: See that the same passenger is at rest for one observer and in motion for another.
instructions: Choose who is watching: the person on the platform or your friend in the train.
Press Play (or drag the time slider).
Watch your position measured from that observer: does it change?
